verification_questions.question: Is there a deterministic unit test in src/store/ that constructs two TaskEvents with IDENTICAL updatedAt and IDENTICAL updatedBy pubkey but DIFFERENT updatedByDevice (the sibling-device case), proves both events are dropped by the current reducer (test fails on master), and proves one event deterministically wins with the new three-level tie-break (test passes after the fix)?

Does the fix add updatedByDevice as the third level in the LWW tie-break (after updatedAt and updatedBy), rather than weakening the reducer back to >= or applying a workaround like timestamp-bumping on the receive path?

Is the three-level tie-break applied identically at ALL 5 enumerated merge gates: the 4 reducer mutation arms in src/store/task-reducer.ts (task.updated lines 19-23, task.status_changed lines 38-41, task.assigned lines 56-59, task.deleted lines 74-77) AND the bootstrap snapshot merge gate in src/marmot/device-sync.ts (fetchAndApplyTaskBootstrap lines 1405-1412)? Cite line numbers in the fix and quote each comparator post-fix to confirm shape-identity.

Is updatedByDevice stamped at a SINGLE chokepoint (dispatch() in task-store.tsx, which already has client in scope via useMarmot()) rather than threaded through every producer (Board.tsx etc)? The accessor is client.keyPackages.clientId per the marmot-ts API.

Does the fix preserve the existing ensureMonotonicTimestamp helper from task-store-utils.ts (the same-device sequential-edit fix from bug task-same-second-edit-dropped)? Specifically, the helper bumps updatedAt only — the new updatedByDevice field must round-trip through the helper's spread return, and the orthogonal ordering axis it addresses must continue to work.

Are persisted events without updatedByDevice (rows already in IndexedDB) decoded correctly and sorted consistently against new events? The agreed backward-compat contract is: missing/undefined updatedByDevice is treated as the empty string and sorts below any real value at the third tie-break level.

Does the full vitest suite pass post-fix, with no regressions vs the recorded baseline test count? Specifically: all existing property-test invariants in task-reducer.property.test.ts (A1-A6, C1, C2, C3, D1, IDEMPOTENCE, COMMUTATIVITY-CREATE-UPDATE) and multi-client.property.test.ts still pass. Baseline counts must be captured from a pre-fix run; final counts from the post-fix run.

Are the property tests in task-reducer.property.test.ts and/or multi-client.property.test.ts broadened to cover the sibling-device case? Specifically: either the scoped C1 invariant at task-reducer.property.test.ts:800-813 (which limits permutation-independence to task.status_changed-only sequences) is widened, OR a new dedicated property test generator produces sibling-device pairs (two actors sharing a pubkey, distinct updatedByDevice) and asserts convergence under arbitrary delivery order.

Is docs/task-protocol.md updated to document the implemented three-level tie-break? The document already references updatedByDevice as 'reserved' in section 7 — the reserved label should be removed and the implemented semantics described, including the backward-compat rule (missing == empty string sorts lowest).

Does TaskEvent round-trip cleanly through the rumor.content JSON serialization at task-store.tsx:312-315 (JSON.stringify) and device-sync.ts:874-876 (JSON.parse) preserving updatedByDevice? Confirmed by either (a) a unit test that round-trips a TaskEvent with updatedByDevice set through stringify/parse, or (b) the e2e suite's existing publish-contract spec passing post-fix.

Layer 2 of the recommended fix — subscribing to the new marmot-ts rollback event in src/marmot/device-sync.ts and re-issuing locally-sent task events from RollbackInfo.appMessages — is either (a) implemented and verified, or (b) explicitly deferred to a follow-up with reasoning recorded in the result.json. Without this layer, sibling-device task events emitted inside an MLS fork window never reach the network, so the new tie-break has nothing to tie-break. Explicit deferral is acceptable; silent omission is not.

Does the Task interface (separate from TaskEvent) in src/store/task-events.ts also carry updatedByDevice, so that the bootstrap snapshot merge gate at device-sync.ts:1405-1412 (which operates on Map<string, Task>, not TaskEvent) can perform the three-level compare? When the reducer applies a winning event, it must propagate event.updatedByDevice into the resulting Task object.
